title: Finite-free algebraic-closure coefficient presentation on the cofinal field tail
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, $E$ a finite intermediate extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$, and $X$ any scheme. Use a small pro-étale site and a coefficient universe containing the site and the set $\Omega$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $S=E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ and $T=\Omega_X=p_X^*\underline\Omega$, with the condensed and pulled-back coefficient conventions [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $I$ be the poset of finite intermediate fields of $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $I_E$ its full subposet on fields containing $E$ [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions]. For an inclusion $H\subseteq J$ write $a_{H,J}:H_X\to J_X$ for the specified coefficient ring map, and $q_H:H_X\to T$ for the specified closure map [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-map, def-sfb-subfield-to-qlbar-coefficient-map].

The posets $I,I_E$ are small in this universe, $I_E$ is nonempty and filtered, and $I_E\hookrightarrow I$ is cofinal: for every $H\in I$, the poset of $F\in I_E$ containing $H$ is nonempty and directed. The maps $a$ compose as the inclusions do, and $q_Ja_{H,J}=q_H$. Every $F_X$, with its $S$-action through $a_{E,F}$, is finite free over $S$, of rank $[F:E]$, including the rank-one identity at $F=E$.

The maps $q_F$ exhibit $T$ as the colimit of $(F_X)_{F\in I_E}$ in sheaves of commutative rings and in sheaves of commutative $S$-algebras, with structure map $q_E$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Explicitly, for any commutative ring sheaf $B$ and compatible ring maps $t_F:F_X\to B$, there is exactly one ring map $t:T\to B$ with $tq_F=t_F$ for every $F\in I_E$; if $B$ is an $S$-algebra and the $t_F$ are $S$-algebra maps, this $t$ is an $S$-algebra map. Under the equivalence preserving underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], these same $q_F$ exhibit the underlying $S$-module of $T$ as the module-sheaf colimit [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with exactly the actions induced by $a_{E,F}$ and $q_E$. No choice of finite bases changes the transitions or cocone legs.

proof.text: The existing finite-intermediate-field directed-order instance supplies a common finite overfield of any two fields. Restrict this construction to the subtype of fields containing E; E itself is an object. Restrict again to fields containing both E and H for the displayed cofinality assertion. Infer smallness from the field subtype, and filteredness from the resulting nonempty directed order. This uses the existing finite-compositum construction without its stronger degree bound or finite-subset assertion.

source.place: Directed finite subextensions; elementary restriction to the tail by composita

proof.text: The point-level transition maps are postcomposition with field inclusions, so $\iota_{H,H}=1$ and $\iota_{J,K}\iota_{H,J}=\iota_{H,K}$. By the definition of $a_{H,J}$ and functoriality of $\Lambda\mapsto\Lambda_X$, their images satisfy $a_{H,H}=1$ and $a_{J,K}a_{H,J}=a_{H,K}$. The coefficient-map compatibility lemma gives $q_Ja_{H,J}=q_H$. In particular $a_{F,G}a_{E,F}=a_{E,G}$ and $q_Fa_{E,F}=q_E$ on the tail; these are precisely the compatibilities for its $S$-algebra structures and for its cocone.

source.place: Opening paragraph, transitions and cocone compatibility; apply the pullback functor

proof.text: Apply cartesianCoefficients_finiteFree to the inclusion E ≤ F. Its first clause supplies an integral basis; its second clause, applied to this basis, supplies the rational comparison isomorphism at X. Reverse that isomorphism to obtain the displayed finite-free witness. The identity-inclusion scalar module is definitionally the self-module, whose finrank is one.

source.place: Integral basis and rational finite-free comparison

proof.text: The inclusion of the tail into all finite intermediate fields is a final functor: for any H, a common finite overfield of E and H lies in the tail above H. Restrict the existing abelian-sheaf coefficient cocone padicAlgClRingObjCocone along this functor. Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv transports isColimitPadicAlgClRingObjCocone to this restricted cocone, with exactly the original closure legs. Bundle the coefficient fields and maps as a diagram of ring objects. Apply Mon.filtered_cocone_isColimit to the underlying abelian colimit. Tensor preserves these colimits since the sheaf tensor functors are left adjoints. For a compatible family t, bundle t as a competing ring-object cocone and use its canonical descent morphism. Its factorization equations and uniqueness, after projecting underlying maps, are exactly the displayed ring universal property. Restricting to commutative targets yields the required commutative ring statement.

source.place: Third isomorphism; explicit extension and restriction of cocones to fields containing E

proof.text: Now give $B$ a commutative $S$-algebra structure $s_B:S\to B$, and suppose the tail maps $t_F$ are $S$-algebra maps. Since the tail contains $E$ and its structure map $a_{E,E}$ is the identity, $t_E=s_B$. The factorization from step 4 satisfies $tq_E=t_E=s_B$, exactly the defining condition for an $S$-algebra map. Its uniqueness as a ring map implies uniqueness as an $S$-algebra map. This proves the asserted algebra colimit with structure map $q_E$.

source.place: Third isomorphism; elementary universal property in the category of S-algebras

proof.text: Apply the already proved qlbar_tail_module_colimit at X, ell and E, and project its final conjunct. Its stage objects, vertex and sectionwise factorization equations are exactly those in the final conjunct here. This avoids repeating the general directed ring-sheaf/module-colimit argument and the internal-module equivalence transport. No basis occurs in the definitions of the transitions or cocone legs.
